category_title: Students with EBD experiencing behavioral outbursts and academic difficulties in science
student_description: Sam is an 11-year-old who loves science but struggles with reading and core academic skills, leading to severe anxiety and outbursts when asked to read aloud or tackle unstructured tasks. He uniquely requires highly structured, reciprocal peer interactions and explicit visual/mnemonic scaffolds to bypass his reading insecurities and maintain behavioral regulation.

criteria.rationale: Sam struggles with core reading skills and needs alternative ways to process and retain science vocabulary without relying on raw text.
criteria.check: The tutor provides or suggests graphic organizers, keyword mnemonics, or visual prompts to help the student organize and learn new concepts.

criteria.rationale: Forcing Sam to read aloud or perform publicly triggers severe anxiety about peer mockery and leads to defensive outbursts.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly avoids asking the student to read aloud in front of peers and provides alternative, private ways to access the text.

criteria.rationale: Unstructured tasks lead to off-task behavior, so Sam needs immediate, tangible incentives to maintain focus during group work.
criteria.check: The tutor utilizes points, rewards, or clear immediate praise specifically tied to the student's positive collaboration and on-task behavior in a group setting.
